warnings: No articles are imported in this database, so every footprint figure in this snapshot is an empty dataset rather than a measurement of low coverage.

unique_stories.label: Unique stories
unique_stories.plain: How many distinct pieces of journalism exist, after collapsing syndicated republications of the same text into one.
unique_stories.counts: One per syndication cluster, plus every article that is in no cluster.
unique_stories.caveat: A cluster is a judgement made by the deduplication pass. Check the cluster list before quoting this figure in a contested setting.

unique_outlets.label: Unique outlets
unique_outlets.plain: How many separate publications carried the story, counting a syndicated republication as a real appearance because a reader of that outlet did see it.
unique_outlets.counts: COUNT(DISTINCT outlet_id) across all articles, before clustering.

total_articles.label: Total articles
total_articles.plain: Every imported item, including syndicated duplicates.
total_articles.counts: Every article row for the campaign within the day-index cutoff.

syndication_ratio.label: Syndication ratio
syndication_ratio.plain: How far the average story travelled. 1.0 means every outlet wrote its own piece; 8.0 means one story reached eight outlets.
syndication_ratio.counts: Unique outlets divided by unique stories.
syndication_ratio.caveat: A high ratio is wire pickup, not independent interest. It inflates outlet counts without adding newsroom attention.

tier_mix.label: Outlet tier mix
tier_mix.plain: Where the coverage sits: national press, trade press, wires, NGO channels and so on.
tier_mix.counts: Articles grouped by their outlet's tier, as counts and as a share of all articles.

country_count.label: Countries
country_count.counts: COUNT(DISTINCT country) over articles, falling back to the outlet's country when the article row has none.
country_count.caveat: Articles with no country on either the article or the outlet are excluded and reported separately as a coverage gap.

language_count.label: Languages
language_count.plain: How many languages the coverage appeared in.
language_count.counts: COUNT(DISTINCT language) over articles, falling back to the outlet's language.

total_reach.label: Total reach where sourced
total_reach.plain: The summed audience of the outlets that carried coverage, counting only outlets whose reach figure comes from a named source.
total_reach.counts: SUM(outlets.reach_value) over distinct outlets with a non-null reach_value.
total_reach.caveat: Always read with the reach coverage percentage. If 20% of outlets have a reach figure, this is 20% of an answer, not a total.

reach_coverage.label: Outlets with a known reach value
reach_coverage.plain: What share of the outlets carrying this campaign have an audience figure from a named source. This is the honesty check on total reach.
reach_coverage.counts: Outlets with a non-null reach_value divided by all outlets carrying the campaign.

peak_day.label: Peak day
peak_day.plain: The day, counted from publication, on which the most articles appeared.
peak_day.counts: The earliest day_index holding the maximum daily article count. Ties go to the earlier day.

peak_volume.label: Peak day volume
peak_volume.plain: How many articles appeared on the busiest day.

days_to_peak.label: Days to peak
days_to_peak.plain: How long the story took to reach its busiest day. Zero means it peaked on publication day.

half_life_days.label: Half-life
half_life_days.plain: How many days after the peak it took for daily volume to fall below a tenth of the peak and stay there — a measure of how quickly the story burned out.
half_life_days.counts: Days from the peak day to the first day whose 3-day trailing mean volume is below 10% of the peak volume.
half_life_days.caveat: Null while a campaign is still running or has not yet decayed. A null is not a zero.

days_to_90pct.label: Days to 90% of volume
days_to_90pct.plain: How long it took to accumulate nine tenths of all the coverage the campaign ever got.
days_to_90pct.counts: The first day index at which cumulative articles reach 90% of the campaign total.
days_to_90pct.caveat: Only meaningful once a campaign has finished. Returns null for live campaigns, because the denominator is not final.

long_tail.label: Long tail
long_tail.plain: Whether the campaign was still producing coverage more than 30 days after publication.
long_tail.counts: True if any article has a day index greater than 30.

own_company_mentions.label: Own-company mentions
own_company_mentions.plain: How many times our own company is named, and in what capacity.
own_company_mentions.counts: Mention rows joining the own_company entity, grouped by role.
own_company_mentions.caveat: Only counts articles whose body text was imported. Exports without full text cannot be scanned for mentions, and that gap is reported alongside.

depth_score.label: Exposure depth
depth_score.plain: How central our company is to the coverage, not just how often it appears. Being the subject of a story counts far more than being listed in passing.
depth_score.counts: Subject x5, named supplier x3, named buyer x3, quoted response x2, passing reference x1, summed across mentions.
depth_score.caveat: Never quote the total on its own. The components are what make it arguable, and they are always returned with it.

first_mention_day.label: First mention
first_mention_day.plain: The day, counted from publication, on which our company was first named.
first_mention_day.counts: The lowest day index among articles containing an own-company mention.

competitor_comparison.label: Named alongside peers
competitor_comparison.plain: Whether we are named more, less, or alongside comparable companies.
competitor_comparison.counts: Mention counts per entity for own_company and competitor entities, side by side.

escalation_count.label: Escalations
escalation_count.plain: How many downstream consequences the campaign has produced: legal petitions, regulatory action, customs measures, buyer statements, parliamentary questions, certifier responses.
escalation_count.counts: Escalation rows for the campaign within the day-index cutoff.
escalation_count.caveat: Manually logged. A zero can mean nothing happened or that nobody logged it; the log's last-updated date is shown alongside.

days_to_first_escalation.label: Days to first escalation
days_to_first_escalation.plain: How long after publication the first downstream consequence appeared. The sharpest early signal of whether a story is going to become a problem.
days_to_first_escalation.counts: Day index of the earliest escalation.

severity_weighted_total.label: Severity-weighted escalation total
severity_weighted_total.plain: Escalations summed by their severity, so one customs measure is not counted the same as one expression of concern.
severity_weighted_total.counts: SUM(severity) across escalations, with the 1-5 anchors listed in the README.

escalation_chain.label: Escalation chain
escalation_chain.plain: How far the campaign travelled along publication to NGO action to regulatory action to buyer action.
escalation_chain.counts: The furthest stage reached, with the first event in each stage and the days it took.

severity_anchors.5: Binding regulatory or customs measure, or litigation filed
